senses.gloss: f. (גול, גלל; cmp. גְּלִימָא) [wrapper,] a long woolen cloak of state used at prayers.
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 77b:11">Sabb. 77ᵇ</cite> (playful etymology) <he>ג׳ גלי ותיב</he> Ar. a. Rashi, roll it up and sit down (Ms. O. <he>גלי ואייתי</he> travel abroad and import it, ed. <he>גלי ואתיב</he> uncover thyself and put it down).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:4:6">Y. Kil. IX, end, 32ᵈ</cite> to wrap up money <he>גו גוֹלְתֵה וכ׳</he> in one’s cloak and tie it up with linen cords.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 3:4:7">Y. Taan. III, 66ᵈ</cite> top <he>עצור גּוֹלְתָךְ וכ׳</he> save thy cloak from the rain (a sneer at an unefficacious prayer for rain). Ib. IV, 67ᶜ <he>את יהב לִי גוֹלְתִי וכ׳</he> give me my cloak that we may pray at the time of closing the gates (sunset).

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 85a:10">B. Mets. 85ᵃ</cite> <he>ג׳ דדהבא וכ׳</he> they spread over thee a gold-trimmed cloak (at graduation ceremonies); a. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="C00408"><he>גּוֹלָתָא</he></cite>, <cite ref="C00395"><he>גּוֹלְיָתָא</he></cite>, <he>גּוֹלְיָין</he>.
<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Numbers 15:38">Targ. Y. II, Num. XV, 38</cite> <he>גוֹלַתְהוֹן</he>, I <he>גּוּלְיַתְהוֹן</he> a. <he>גּוּלֵיהוֹן</he>.
<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Numbers 16:1">Targ. Y. ib. XVI, 1</cite> <he>גּוֹלְיָיתֵיה</he> his cloaks.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 22:12">Targ. Y. I Deut. XXII, 12</cite> <he>גּוֹלְיַית־</he>, II <he>גּוֹלָתֵי־</he>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 36">Gen. R. s. 36</cite> (expl. <he>סרבלי־</he> <cite ref="Daniel 3:21">Dan. III, 21</cite>) <he>בגוּלֵיהוֹן</he> (fr. <he>גּוֹלָא</he>) in their fine cloaks; <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:9">Cant. R. to VII, 9</cite>; <cite ref="Esther Rabbah 3:14">Esth. R. to I, 12</cite>.

<cite ref="Beitzah 38b:1">Bets. 38ᵇ</cite> <he>גּוֹלָתַיְיכִי שקלי</he> have I taken your cloaks (that you laugh at me)?—[<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 19">Gen. R. s. 19</cite> <he>גולין</he> Ar. ed. Koh., v. <cite ref="C00941"><he>גִּלָּיוֹן</he></cite> end.]
